$comment: The platform's list of what it must not break — consumer-conformance.yml builds and tests
each entry against every platform PR touching src/**. A product that is not registered here
gets no protection, which is the incentive to register. Keep it small and honest: every entry
costs CI minutes on every platform PR, so mark a consumer 'conformance': false with a note
rather than deleting the signal that it exists.

consumers.note: Reference product for module, role, approval, document, and RAG seams. Consumes Plenipo.* alpha.28 from the vendored .packages feed; the alpha.29 upgrade (CSP nonce, the Plenipo.Testing kit, six retired shims) is networthy#247.

Real Plenipo.* consumer (alpha.28). Its two prerequisites landed with auditworthy#27 (central PlenipoVersion; Microsoft.Extensions.AI 10.8.1 on main). The alpha.29 upgrade is auditworthy#101 — flip conformance on when it reports green against alpha.29.

Real Plenipo.* consumer (alpha.28) on main — src/Hireworthy.{AppHost,Host,Hiring} verified via the GitHub tree — and it filed #145 with an L3 reproduction, so it was consuming the platform while unregistered and therefore unprotected. Registered with conformance OFF deliberately, not as a judgement on the repo: #144 documents that one red consumer deadlocks every platform PR, so adding an unproven consumer to the blocking matrix while that is live would widen a known deadlock. The alpha.29 upgrade is hireworthy#66; flip conformance on once #144 is fixed AND it reports green against alpha.29.
